Model registry

Source: MODELS.md

This file is the single source of truth for every model and formula in trainingmodels. Function documentation, pkgdown articles, the Shiny app texts and the software paper are derived from it and must not contradict it.

Rules

  1. A formula is implemented only after its entry here reaches status verified and the author has approved it (decision D-003).
  2. Every entry states which source the formula was checked against and how. A secondary source alone is never enough for verified.
  3. Disagreements found between sources are recorded in the discrepancy log, not silently resolved.
  4. Reference values listed here are the numerical targets for unit tests.

Status vocabulary

Status Meaning
verified Formula checked against the source named in the entry; reference values reproduced independently
partly verified Checked against an author’s code or a peer-reviewed secondary source; the original article has not been read
unverified Known only from secondary sources that have not been cross-checked
planned / implemented Development state, independent of verification

How verification was done so far. Sources were read as Markdown conversions of the PDFs supplied by the package author, not from the PDFs themselves. A conversion can introduce transcription errors (the Morton 1990 conversion notes one restored + sign in Eq. 7), so equations that matter were additionally checked by recomputing published numbers. Reviews were drafted with Claude (Anthropic) in chat; see AI_USAGE.md. Author approval of each entry is recorded in the entry.

M-01 Exponential filter and the two timing conventions

Status: verified (both conventions) · implemented in 0.0.3 Author approval: approved 2026-11-24 (entry as written; verification status unchanged) · amendment of 2026-11-27 (initial state): approved 2026-11-27

The literature uses two different discrete forms. They are not equivalent and the package offers both through the argument same_day_load = c("exclude", "include"). The default is "exclude" (decisions D-011 and D-012).

Convention “include” (Morton, Fitz-Clarke & Banister 1990, Eqs. 4-5). The load of day tt counts on day tt at full weight; values refer to the end of day tt.

ginc(t)=ginc(t−1)e−1/τ+w(t)=∑s=1tw(s)e−(t−s)/τ g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) = g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t-1)\,e^{-1/\tau} + w(t) = \sum_{s=1}^{t} w(s)\,e^{-(t-s)/\tau}

Convention “exclude” (Busso lineage; sum to t−1t-1). The load of day tt does not affect day tt; yesterday’s load is already attenuated by e−1/τe^{-1/\tau}.

gexc(t)=∑s=1t−1w(s)e−(t−s)/τ,gexc(t)=[gexc(t−1)+w(t−1)]e−1/τ g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = \sum_{s=1}^{t-1} w(s)\,e^{-(t-s)/\tau}, \qquad g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = \left[g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t-1) + w(t-1)\right] e^{-1/\tau}

Exact relationship (derived here and checked numerically):

ginc(t)=gexc(t)+w(t),gexc(t+1)=e−1/τginc(t) g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) = g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) + w(t), \qquad g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t+1) = e^{-1/\tau}\,g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t)

Consequences

  • Gains kk fitted under one convention are not comparable with gains fitted under the other. Every fitted object must store and print its convention.
  • The difference matters most when a performance test and a training session fall on the same day. “exclude” corresponds to a test done before that day’s training; “include” to a value at the end of the day.
  • Morton et al. (1990) state that the criterion performance was usually done at the beginning of a training bout, yet their Eqs. 4-5 include that day’s load.

Verification

Convention Checked against How
include Morton et al. 1990, Eqs. 4-9, Figs. 3-4 Worked example recomputed (see M-02 reference values)
include Clarke & Skiba 2013, supplemental spreadsheet, sheets 6, 8, 9 Spreadsheet formulas read; modelled performance on the 9 test days of sheet 8 reproduced exactly
exclude Busso & Chalencon 2023, Supplemental Digital Content 2 (R script) Matrix algebra of the script emulated with random loads; equals the sum to t−1t-1
exclude Vermeire et al. 2022; Imbach et al. 2022 (Eq. 1); Marchal et al. 2025 Equation as printed

Notes

  • Morton’s Eqs. 4-5 allow any spacing ii between sessions, including several sessions per day. The package aggregates to one value per day; this is a simplification of Morton’s formulation.
  • Initial state is g(0)=h(0)=0g(0) = h(0) = 0 unless set by the user (D-025). Morton et al. assigned an initial fitness of 1,000 units to one subject.

Initial state (amendment 2026-11-27; derived here, not taken from a source). With initial value g(0)=g0g(0) = g_0, both conventions add g0e−t/τg_0\,e^{-t/\tau} to day tt:

ginc(t)=g0e−t/τ+∑s=1tw(s)e−(t−s)/τ,gexc(t)=g0e−t/τ+∑s=1t−1w(s)e−(t−s)/τ g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) = g_0\,e^{-t/\tau} + \sum_{s=1}^{t} w(s)\,e^{-(t-s)/\tau}, \qquad g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = g_0\,e^{-t/\tau} + \sum_{s=1}^{t-1} w(s)\,e^{-(t-s)/\tau}

so that ginc(1)=g0e−1/τ+w(1)g_{\mathrm{inc}}(1) = g_0\,e^{-1/\tau} + w(1) and gexc(1)=g0e−1/τg_{\mathrm{exc}}(1) = g_0\,e^{-1/\tau}. The recursions of M-01 start from g(0)=g0g(0) = g_0 (with w(0)=0w(0) = 0 under “exclude”), and the identities ginc(t)=gexc(t)+w(t)g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) = g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) + w(t) and gexc(t+1)=e−1/τginc(t)g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t+1) = e^{-1/\tau}\,g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) still hold.

M-02 Two-component impulse-response model (Banister)

Status: verified · simulation implemented in 0.0.3; fit planned for 0.1.0 Author approval: approved 2026-11-24 (entry as written; verification status unchanged)

p(t)=p0+k1g(t)−k2h(t) p(t) = p_0 + k_1\,g(t) - k_2\,h(t)

with gg and hh the filters of M-01 with time constants τ1\tau_1 and τ2\tau_2.

  • Morton et al. (1990, Eq. 8) write p(t)=k1g(t)−k2h(t)p(t) = k_1 g(t) - k_2 h(t) with no baseline. Their p(t)p(t) is on an arbitrary scale and is related to criterion points by least-squares regression, and k1k_1 is 1 for both subjects in their Table 2.
  • The form with an explicit baseline and five free parameters is the one used by Busso & Chalencon (2023), Vermeire et al. (2022), Imbach et al. (2022) and Marchal et al. (2025).
  • Attribution: the two-component model is commonly cited as Banister et al. (1975). That article has not been read. Until it is, cite Calvert et al.
    1. and Morton et al. (1990) for the model and treat 1975 as historical origin only.

Reference values, convention “include” (Morton et al. 1990, Figs. 3-4; w=100w = 100 per day from day 1, τ1=45\tau_1 = 45, τ2=15\tau_2 = 15, k1=1k_1 = 1, k2=2k_2 = 2, no baseline):

Quantity Published Recomputed
k1g(60)k_1 g(60) 3,351 3,350.8
k2h(60)k_2 h(60) 3,044 3,044.3
Asymptote of k1gk_1 g 4,550 4,550.2
Asymptote of k2hk_2 h 3,101 3,101.1
Asymptote of pp 1,449 1,449.1
Day of minimum pp 16 16 (Eq. 10 gives 16.09)

Peak after stopping from steady state 2,121, 16 days later 2,121.4, 16 days later

Reference fit, convention “include” (Clarke & Skiba 2013, Fig. 8 and supplemental sheet 8; one cyclist, 166 days, 9 tests): p0=261.93p_0 = 261.93, k1=0.18258k_1 = 0.18258, k2=0.23016k_2 = 0.23016, τ1=35.821\tau_1 = 35.821, τ2=21.340\tau_2 = 21.340; recomputed R2=0.979R^2 = 0.979 (published 0.98). The supplemental data are not redistributed with the package; they are used only as an external check.

Limitations to document (sources in brackets): parameters are strongly correlated and several parameter sets fit equally well [Hellard 2006, not yet read; Busso & Chalencon 2023, SDC 3; Vermeire 2022, Table 1]; results depend on starting values with local optimisers [Vermeire 2022]; adding fatigue improved fit but not prediction in two datasets [Marchal 2025]; with 56-104 tests per swimmer the mean R2R^2 of the model was 0.29, and the mean absolute percentage error of its predictions was 2.0% and 2.7% in two validation sets [Busso & Chalencon 2023]; the positive effect is linear in training load, so the model cannot represent maladaptation to overtraining, and an optimal training load before a taper cannot be searched with it [Busso & Chalencon 2023]; optimising the model without constraints gives maximal training followed by rest [Ceddia 2025, preprint].

M-04 Response to constant daily training

Status: verified for convention “include” · implemented in 0.0.3 Author approval: approved 2026-11-24 (entry as written; verification status unchanged) · amendment of 2026-11-27 (convention “exclude”, existence, reference values): approved 2026-11-27, after correcting the asymptote under “exclude”

For w(t)=Tw(t) = T every day from day 1 (Morton et al. 1990, Eqs. 6, 9-11):

ginc(t)=T1−e−t/τ1−e−1/τ,p(∞)=k1T1−e−1/τ1−k2T1−e−1/τ2 g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) = T\,\frac{1 - e^{-t/\tau}}{1 - e^{-1/\tau}}, \qquad p(\infty) = \frac{k_1 T}{1 - e^{-1/\tau_1}} - \frac{k_2 T}{1 - e^{-1/\tau_2}}

Day of poorest performance (Morton’s tnt_n, Eq. 10; rederived here):

tmin=τ1τ2τ1−τ2ln⁡[τ1k2(1−e−1/τ1)τ2k1(1−e−1/τ2)] t_{\min} = \frac{\tau_1 \tau_2}{\tau_1 - \tau_2}\, \ln\!\left[\frac{\tau_1 k_2 \left(1 - e^{-1/\tau_1}\right)} {\tau_2 k_1 \left(1 - e^{-1/\tau_2}\right)}\right]

Under convention “exclude” (derived here, not taken from a source):

gexc(t)=Te−1/τ1−e−(t−1)/τ1−e−1/τ g_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = T\,e^{-1/\tau}\,\frac{1 - e^{-(t-1)/\tau}}{1 - e^{-1/\tau}}

Amendment 2026-11-27 (derived here, not taken from a source):

  • The day of poorest performance tmint_{\min} is the same under “exclude”: gexc(t)=ginc(t)−Tg_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) - T for constant training, so both forms have the same derivative in tt.
  • The asymptote is not the same. Since gexc(t)=ginc(t)−Tg_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = g_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) - T, pexc(∞)=pinc(∞)−(k1−k2)Tp_{\mathrm{exc}}(\infty) = p_{\mathrm{inc}}(\infty) - (k_1 - k_2)\,T:

pinc(∞)=p0+k1T1−e−1/τ1−k2T1−e−1/τ2,pexc(∞)=p0+k1Te−1/τ11−e−1/τ1−k2Te−1/τ21−e−1/τ2 p_{\mathrm{inc}}(\infty) = p_0 + \frac{k_1 T}{1 - e^{-1/\tau_1}} - \frac{k_2 T}{1 - e^{-1/\tau_2}}, \qquad p_{\mathrm{exc}}(\infty) = p_0 + \frac{k_1 T\,e^{-1/\tau_1}}{1 - e^{-1/\tau_1}} - \frac{k_2 T\,e^{-1/\tau_2}}{1 - e^{-1/\tau_2}}

  • tmint_{\min} exists only if τ1>τ2\tau_1 > \tau_2 and the argument of the logarithm is >1> 1; otherwise it is NA (D-026). It also needs k1>0k_1 > 0: with k1=0k_1 = 0 the argument is infinite and performance only falls (as in M-05).

Reference values, convention “exclude” (Morton’s example, M-02; w=100w = 100 per day from day 1, τ1=45\tau_1 = 45, τ2=15\tau_2 = 15, k1=1k_1 = 1, k2=2k_2 = 2, no baseline; recomputed here): k1g(60)=3250.7694k_1 g(60) = 3250.7694, k2h(60)=2844.3122k_2 h(60) = 2844.3122, minimum of pp on day 16.

M-05 Response to a single session (influence curve)

Status: partly verified · implemented in 0.0.3 Author approval: approved 2026-11-24 (entry as written; verification status unchanged) · amendment of 2026-11-27 (convention, existence, reference values): approved 2026-11-27, including the condition k1>0k_1 > 0

Effect on performance uu days after one unit of load:

L(u)=k1e−u/τ1−k2e−u/τ2 L(u) = k_1\,e^{-u/\tau_1} - k_2\,e^{-u/\tau_2}

tn=τ1τ2τ1−τ2ln⁡(k2k1),tg=τ1τ2τ1−τ2ln⁡(k2τ1k1τ2) t_n = \frac{\tau_1 \tau_2}{\tau_1 - \tau_2}\,\ln\!\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right), \qquad t_g = \frac{\tau_1 \tau_2}{\tau_1 - \tau_2}\, \ln\!\left(\frac{k_2\,\tau_1}{k_1\,\tau_2}\right)

tnt_n: days until the net effect of the session becomes positive. tgt_g: days until it is largest. Both were rederived here. Printed in Clarke & Skiba (2013, Fig. 8B), Busso & Chalencon (2023, Eqs. 12-13) and Ceddia et al. (2025, Eqs. 3-4, as trt_r and tpt_p). The original, Fitz-Clarke, Morton & Banister (1991), has not been read.

Amendment 2026-11-27 (derived here, not taken from a source):

  • tnt_n and tgt_g do not depend on the timing convention. Only the effect on the day of the session does: k1−k2k_1 - k_2 under “include”, 0 under “exclude”. For u≥1u \ge 1 both conventions give L(u)L(u).
  • Existence, for τ1>τ2\tau_1 > \tau_2: tnt_n (time_to_recover) exists if k2>k1k_2 > k_1; tgt_g (time_to_peak) exists if k2τ1>k1τ2k_2\,\tau_1 > k_1\,\tau_2. Both also need k1>0k_1 > 0: with k1=0k_1 = 0 the effect is never positive and the logarithms are infinite. If τ1≤τ2\tau_1 \le \tau_2, or for the fitness-only model (M-03), both are NA (D-026).

Reference values for Morton’s parameters (k1=1k_1 = 1, k2=2k_2 = 2, τ1=45\tau_1 = 45, τ2=15\tau_2 = 15; recomputed here): tn=15.5958t_n = 15.5958 days, tg=40.3146t_g = 40.3146 days, effect at the peak L(tg)=0.272166L(t_g) = 0.272166 per unit of load.

Name clash. Morton et al. (1990) use tnt_n for a different quantity: the day of poorest performance under constant daily training (M-04). Function and argument names must not use a bare t_n. Names (D-026): time_to_recover (tnt_n here), time_to_peak (tgt_g), time_of_minimum (M-04).

Recommendation to document: In Busso & Chalencon (2023), alternative parameter sets with a similar fit gave small, although statistically significant, differences in the response to a session; the authors recommend characterising an athlete by that response rather than by each parameter taken individually [Busso & Chalencon 2023, Discussion and SDC 3].

M-06 Variable dose-response model (Busso)

Status: partly verified · planned, phase 2 Author approval: approved 2026-11-24 (entry as written; verification status unchanged)

p(n)=p0+k1∑i=1n−1w(i)e−(n−i)/τ1−∑i=1n−1k2(i)w(i)e−(n−i)/τ2,k2(i)=k3∑j=1iw(j)e−(i−j)/τ3 p(n) = p_0 + k_1 \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} w(i)\,e^{-(n-i)/\tau_1} - \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} k_2(i)\,w(i)\,e^{-(n-i)/\tau_2}, \qquad k_2(i) = k_3 \sum_{j=1}^{i} w(j)\,e^{-(i-j)/\tau_3}

Checked against the R script of Busso & Chalencon (2023, SDC 2) by numerical emulation, and against the equations printed in Clarke & Skiba (2013). The fatigue term multiplies by w(i)w(i) and the inner sum runs to ii inclusive. The original article, Busso (2003), has not been read. Two secondary sources print other versions (see discrepancy log).

M-09 Training impulse (TRIMP)

Status: partly verified, with an open discrepancy · not in the first version Author approval: approved 2026-11-24 (entry as written; verification status unchanged)

Morton et al. (1990, Eqs. 1-3):

w=D⋅x⋅ebx,x=HRex−HRrestHRmax−HRrest w = D \cdot x \cdot e^{b x}, \qquad x = \frac{\mathrm{HR_{ex}} - \mathrm{HR_{rest}}}{\mathrm{HR_{max}} - \mathrm{HR_{rest}}}

with DD the duration in minutes, b=1.92b = 1.92 for men and 1.671.67 for women. Clarke & Skiba (2013), citing Banister (1991), print the weighting as 0.64e1.92x0.64\,e^{1.92x} and 0.86e1.67x0.86\,e^{1.67x}. The factors 0.64 and 0.86 do not appear in Morton et al. (1990). To be resolved before implementation.

M-10 Session RPE load

Status: verified · implemented in 0.0.2 Author approval: approved 2026-11-26

w=RPE×D w = \mathrm{RPE} \times D

  • RPE on the 0-10 category-ratio scale: one global rating for the whole session, asked about 30 minutes after it ends.
  • DD: duration in minutes of the entire session, including warm-up, cool-down and recovery intervals.
  • Sessions of the same day are summed (as for every load; see as_daily_load()).

M-11 Rolling load

Status: verified · implemented in 0.0.2 Author approval: approved 2026-11-26

For daily loads w(1),…,w(T)w(1), \dots, w(T) of one athlete and a window of kk days:

Sinc(t)=∑j=t−k+1tw(j),t≥k;Sexc(t)=∑j=t−kt−1w(j),t≥k+1 S_{\mathrm{inc}}(t) = \sum_{j=t-k+1}^{t} w(j), \quad t \ge k; \qquad S_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = \sum_{j=t-k}^{t-1} w(j), \quad t \ge k + 1

  • Rolling mean =S(t)/k= S(t) / k.
  • S(t)S(t) is NA where it is not defined or where any day in the window is missing (D-016).
  • Identity: Sexc(t)=Sinc(t−1)S_{\mathrm{exc}}(t) = S_{\mathrm{inc}}(t-1).
  • Timing option same_day_load as in D-020; default "include" (D-021).

M-12 Monotony and strain

Status: verified · implemented in 0.0.2 Author approval: approved 2026-11-26

Foster (1998):

monotony=mean daily load of the weekSD of the daily loads of the week,strain=weekly load×monotony \text{monotony} = \frac{\text{mean daily load of the week}} {\text{SD of the daily loads of the week}}, \qquad \text{strain} = \text{weekly load} \times \text{monotony}

  • SD is the sample standard deviation (n−1n - 1).
  • Assumption, not stated by Foster: rest days count as load 0.
  • Package generalisation: the week is a rolling window of kk days (default 7) under either timing option of M-11 (D-022). When all loads in the window are equal the SD is 0 and monotony and strain are NA.

Verification

17 Foster 1998 Table 1 Monotony printed as 1.44; the value is 1.449 (truncated). The printed strain 5397 agrees with the unrounded monotony Recalculation

Data requirements and published designs

All impulse-response models in this registry need the same data: one load value per day and performance on some days. Example datasets shipped with the package are simulated and labelled as such.

Design Source Features
Overload then detraining Morton et al. 1990 28 days of daily or twice-daily training, then 50 days without formal training; best-effort test at least twice a week; 2 subjects
In-season monitoring Busso & Chalencon 2023 Two tests per week over one or two seasons; 56-104 tests per swimmer
Teaching laboratory Clarke & Skiba 2013 Tests at least weekly, 3-15 min maximal efforts, in all phases of training
